doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Semi-retirement, Japan trips and playing for pleasure
summary: He is mostly retired, no longer cares about the woodwinds, goes to Japan with bands about yearly and turns down casual dances.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well what are you up to these days?

Well I’m pretty much retired now. I’ve actually gone exactly the opposite direction than I was for those 20 years I was working in the studios. I don’t really care about playing the woodwinds anymore at all. I don’t bother with them unless I know in advance something’s coming up that I want to do and then I’ll have to spend a week or so woodshedding, so I’ll be okay. I’ve been going to Japan for the last 20 years off and on, with a number of different bands, which I enjoy. I enjoy the trips in Japan. And so I do that usually once a year. This year, ‘99 at this point I don’t know that I’m going. But I’m still playing as much as I can. I still practice and I play with friends as much as I can, and I actually turn down most casual type engagements, like dances or that kind of thing, because I don’t really enjoy them and I don’t have to, I don’t need to do it. So that’s about it. I’m just trying to keep myself together and keep myself healthy so I can last a few more years.
